slides.headline: 6 AI PROMPTS FOR THE EMAILS KEEPING YOU UP
1) RAISE YOUR PRICES WITHOUT LOSING A CLIENT
slides.body: Consultants charge $500 just to script this conversation. "I'm raising [service] from [old price] to [new price]. Write an email that makes the client feel they're getting more, not paying more"

slides.headline: 2) COLLECT LATE PAYMENTS WITHOUT BURNING BRIDGES
slides.body: A collections agency takes 25-50% of what they recover. "My client owes [amount], [days] overdue. Write a reminder firm enough to get paid, warm enough to keep them"

slides.headline: 3) PITCH A STRANGER AND GET A MEETING
slides.body: The average cold email gets a 1% reply rate. "I run [business]. My ideal client is [describe them]. Write a cold email so specific they think I already know them"

slides.headline: 4) FIRE SOMEONE WITHOUT GETTING SUED
slides.body: A lawyer charges $350 an hour to draft this. "I need to let go of [role] for [reason]. Write the email so it's kind, professional, and keeps me legally safe"

slides.headline: 5) RESPOND TO AN ANGRY CUSTOMER AND KEEP THEM
slides.body: Losing one customer costs 5x more than winning a new one. "A customer sent this complaint: [their message]. Write a response that makes them feel heard and want to stay"

slides.headline: 6) REJECT A CLIENT WITHOUT MAKING AN ENEMY
slides.body: A wrong client costs more than no client at all. "I can't take on [project] because [reason]. Write a rejection that leaves the door open and earns their respect"

slides.headline: SAVE THIS POST
slides.body: You'll want these prompts the next time you're staring at a blank draft at midnight. Save it now. Daily AI news and real skills you can use tonight

caption:
Swipe for 6 prompts that write the emails you've been avoiding 👇 Each one nails the tone that gets replies, keeps clients, and closes deals

Raise your prices without losing a client, collect late payments without burning bridges, pitch a cold stranger and land a meeting, fire someone without getting sued, respond to an angry customer and keep them, reject a client without making an enemy

Every business owner has at least one email sitting unsent right now. These prompts handle the ones worth losing sleep over. The owners using them send in 30 seconds instead of drafting for three days.
